newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Shaky Australian stocks end down, eye Wall St.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Shaky Australian stocks end down, eye Wall St.

text.p: Australian shares ended sharply lower on Friday with the negative lead from nervous U.S. markets translating into losses across the board.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 29.4 points lower at 2,423.2.
The March share index futures contract was 36 points lower at 2,416, a 7.2 point discount to the underlying index.

In the face of a 2.3 percent drop in the Dow as U.S. investors fretted over potential interest rate hikes, sellers had control of the local market right from the outset with no sector escaping the axe.
"It was unlikely to go any other way," said a dealer at a Perth-based brokerage.
"That sort of fall has to hurt sentiment no matter what the local values are."

While the market bounced off the bottom late in the day, brokers remained unconvinced and said Wall Street's showing later today and early next week was the key to whether the Dow's seemingly never-ending uptrend had been broken.
"Obviously tonight and next week in the U.S. will be important. The (local) market will need to reassess their reaction after that," said a Brisbane broker.
In the industrial leaders, U.S.-leveraged media group News Corp headed the losers, sliding 1.6 percent to A$6.67.
Global mining giant CRA led the miners lower, shedding 1.4 percent to close at A$18.92.
Bucking the trend was Cultus Petroleum whose shares jumped to a record high A$2.86 before easing to close 18 cents higher at A$2.77 despite a softer first half net profit of A$3.43 million.
Brokers said an optimistic outlook on the stock's exploration programme rather than the profit had been driving its impressive 1997 performance.
The results season had its final day with retail franchisor Harvey Norman posting an 8.4 percent higher first half net profit of A$18.14 million. Its shares ended unchanged at A$6.30 in thin trade.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of nearly four to one, while only 26 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade boomed as traders rushed to cover positions while options activity continued to be moderately active.
Total options traded 36,769 (37,682)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 11,293 (7,471)

In other local markets, the Australian dollar traded above US$0.8000 for the first time in three months and strode to fresh four year highs against the yen as one European buyer bought the currency in volume, said to be at least A$500 million. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT) the dollar was at US$0.7995/00, ending well up an opening US$0.7930/35 and Thursday's US$0.7911/16 local close.
Australian bond yields spiked sharply higher with yesterday's firm tone proving short-lived amid growing expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will tighten policy.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.96 percent, sharply up on Thursday's 7.81 percent.
